briefing.text: On News, Information Technology stays on top with buzz 83.4 (down 3.6 on the day, up 3.4 on the week) and mentions down 64%, led by NVDA, MSFT, AMD, ORCL and QCOM; Financials and Materials each lost 9.5 points of buzz. On X, Information Technology is flat at 93.0 (NVDA, MU, IREN), while Healthcare (VBIO, OBX) rose 10.0 points on mentions up 160% and Real Estate (OPEN, KIM, PK) gained 4.1 on mentions up 237%. On Reddit, Information Technology is first at 92.2 (down 1.4, mentions down 52%, sentiment 0.01), Financial Services rose 5.5 on mentions up 127% (index-fund tickers such as VIMAX, VBTLX), and Utilities and Materials slipped 3.2 and 2.6.

SMMT #1: one article, a MarketBeat note on the share price crossing its 200-day average; it does not explain the rank (price is up 15% and FDA-decision markets exist).
MNDY #2: six articles, mostly a Docusign comparison and a fall below the 50-day average; the rank comes more from earnings on 11-09 and open interest than from news.
LYFT #3: a DoorDash partnership story and a long-term-investor piece; it fits the high attention, but the app-download market is the bigger driver.
CELH #4: reported EPS of $0.41, ahead of consensus per MarketBeat, and the stock is up 7%; this largely explains the rank.
HIMS #5: only a Motley Fool comparison article; earnings on 11-09 and an 8% gain matter more.
FSLR #7: a fund-holding note and a solar-stocks list; the rank is driven by a 15% five-day gain and volume, not by news.
TTWO #8: GTA VI preorders reported at $751 million two weeks before release, plus earnings on 11-09; this explains the rank.
LOW #9: fund-holding and home-improvement list stories (12 articles); routine coverage ahead of 11-18 earnings.

SMMT ranks first on strong attention (94.6th percentile), attention on X (92.8th), a 3.0-sigma price move (+15% in 24h) and volume above normal. MNDY is second on volume (96.6th percentile), open interest (99.2nd) and the 11-09 earnings catalyst, though its attention on X is low. LYFT is third with the highest volume percentile (100th) and attention on X at the 96.4th percentile, with a 0.9-sigma move and falling open interest. SMMT and CELH only just entered the top 20 from far lower ranks, so the order is sensitive to one day of data.

notes: Ranks are by the scoring of record (pick_rank, w2). Prices and moves as of the last pull of the day. Facts from public data; not investment advice.
